statement:
Our EUR trial balance values the GBP bank account differently from treasury's hand calculation on some dates, although both use the same monthly rate file (`examples/rates_2024_03.csv`) and the same postings.

    >>> from datetime import date
    >>> from ledgerly import Account, Chart, Entry, Ledger, Line, Money, importers, reports
    >>> rates = importers.parse_rates_csv(open("examples/rates_2024_03.csv").read())
    >>> ledger = Ledger(Chart([Account("1010", "Bank GBP", "asset"),
    ...                        Account("4000", "Sales", "income")]), rates)
    >>> for eid, on, amount in (("R-1", date(2024, 3, 5), "5000"), ("R-2", date(2024, 3, 20), "3000")):
    ...     m = Money(amount, "GBP")
    ...     ledger.post(Entry(eid, on, [Line("1010", m), Line("4000", -m)]))
    >>> reports.format_money(ledger.balance_in("1010", date(2024, 3, 21)))
    '9,342.76 EUR'          # treasury: 9,318.06 EUR

Balances early in the month agree. Treasury follows the documented rate rules.

Constraints: the rate file comes from our provider as-is and must not be edited. The tests under `tests/` are owned by QA and are read-only; do not modify them. Make sure the existing test suite still passes.
notes: Root cause: RateTable.add appends a rate for an earlier date to the end of the pair's series instead of inserting it in date order, while lookups bisect assuming ascending dates. A late correction in the provider file therefore yields the wrong rate for dates after it. Fix: keep the series sorted on insertion (replace on the same date). Sorting only at lookup leaves history() and saved files unsorted; sorting only the file rows leaves direct out-of-order adds wrong. ANALYSIS ONLY: never shown to agents.
